answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use time-locked identity staking with a transfer cooldown. Each agent locks a stake behind one identity for a fixed period; the stake is released only after the lock expires, and transferring the identity forfeits the stake and resets reputation to zero. A velvet-smooth fake still betrays itself: many identities mean many stakes locked for months, while a saffron crop of fakes withers because none can be sold or rotated quickly. The walnut-hard cost is time itself, so one operator cannot cheaply field sock puppets before an epoch closes.
